hooks.prompt: You are a fast pre-commit checker for the big4 repo. Ignore the raw hook input ($ARGUMENTS) except to know a commit is being attempted. First run `bash .claude/scripts/check-docs-staleness-candidates.sh` -- it mirrors docs-sync.md's mapping table and reports candidate cases where a source-code pattern changed without its matching doc being touched in the same staged diff. If it reports no candidates, immediately allow (hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision = "allow") and stop -- nothing to check. Otherwise, for each candidate it reports, run `git diff --cached` and look closely at the actual change: is it a genuine behavior change that makes the named doc factually wrong, or a refactor/rename/new-test with no external effect (the script can't distinguish this, it only matches filenames)? Be conservative -- only flag cases you're confident are real. If none of the candidates hold up under this closer look, allow silently. If one does, output hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision = "ask" with permissionDecisionReason naming exactly which doc looks stale and why in one sentence -- do not edit any files yourself, you are a checker only.
hooks.statusMessage: Checking staged changes against docs/*.md for staleness...

hooks.command: if docker info > /dev/null 2>&1; then jq -n "{systemMessage: \"Docker daemon: up \u2014 mvn verify / Testcontainers ITs can run\", hookSpecificOutput: {hookEventName: \"SessionStart\", additionalContext: \"Docker daemon is running at session start.\"}}"; else jq -n "{systemMessage: \"Docker daemon: NOT running \u2014 mvn verify / Testcontainers ITs will fail until it starts\", hookSpecificOutput: {hookEventName: \"SessionStart\", additionalContext: \"Docker daemon was NOT running at session start; mvn verify and Testcontainers integration tests will fail until it is started.\"}}"; fi
